lessons.title: if as an Expression
lessons.content: Unlike Java, Kotlin's if can be used as an expression that returns a value, replacing the ternary operator entirely. Real scenario: assigning a value directly from an if/else instead of declaring a var and mutating it in each branch.

codeSnippets.code:
val max = if (a > b) a else b

val status = if (code == 200) "OK" else "Error $code"

lessons.title: when Expression
lessons.content: when replaces Java's switch but is far more powerful - ranges, type checks (is), multiple values per branch, and exhaustive handling over sealed classes. Real scenario: routing a sealed UiState to the right Composable, compiler-enforced.

lessons.title: for Loop
lessons.content: Kotlin's for loop iterates over anything with an iterator - ranges, collections, arrays. Real scenario: iterating with index access via withIndex() for staggered list animations.

codeSnippets.code:
for (item in listOf("a", "b", "c")) println(item)
for ((index, item) in listOf("x", "y").withIndex()) println("$index: $item")

lessons.title: while Loop
lessons.content: while checks its condition before each iteration, running zero or more times. Real scenario: polling a job status endpoint until it reports 'complete'.

lessons.title: do-while Loop
lessons.content: do-while runs the loop body at least once before checking the condition. Real scenario: showing a CLI menu once before checking whether the user chose to exit.

lessons.title: break and continue
lessons.content: break exits a loop entirely; continue skips to the next iteration. Real scenario: skipping invalid records (continue) and stopping a search loop once a match is found (break).

lessons.title: Labels for Nested Loops
lessons.content: A label (name@) lets break/continue target an outer loop from inside a nested one. Real scenario: breaking out of both loops of a 2D grid search entirely once a target cell is found.

lessons.title: Ranges: .., until, downTo, step
lessons.content: Ranges express a sequence of values: 1..5 (inclusive), 1 until 5 (exclusive), 5 downTo 1 (descending), step n to skip values. Real scenario: generating page numbers for pagination UI.
